title: Release week orientation manifest and hourly beat
content:
Purpose
This doc is a compact orientation manifest for the week-of release. Designed for the release conductor, on-call operators, SRE liaisons, and product owners who need an hour-by-hour operational beat plus the pragmatic checklists and communications to keep a low-friction launch.

Goals for the week
- Ship with confidence: keep user-facing latency and error budgets within the agreed SLOs.
- Minimize blast radius: progressive traffic shifts, strict canary windows, and clear rollback gates.
- Capture learnings: quick retro notes at each major milestone.

Quick context
- Release: 2026-06 platform runtime patch + model routing policy update.
- Primary risk: model fallback mismatch causing a high-latency path for 512-token requests.
- Canary cohort: 2% global traffic (regionally split: US 1.2%, EU 0.6%, APAC 0.2%).
- Primary observability: latency_p50/p95, error_rate_5m, kv-cache-hit-rate, queue_depth, pod_restart_rate.

Orientation checklist (pre-start, T-72 to T-2 hours)
- Owners assigned and acknowledged: release_conductor, obs_lead, saas_owner, infra_owner. (Owner rota attached in Confluence).
- Feature flags and traffic rules validated in staging with synthetic load.
- Smoke harness ready: warm caches, warmup traffic, and a 15-minute synthetic acceptance test.
- Backout artifacts staged: canary-toggle, immediate rollback playbook, and emergency traffic re-route runbook.
- Pager templates drafted and test-notifications executed to validate routing.
- Slack channel created: #release-2026-06-runtime (pinned: runbook, key queries, contact map).
- Cross-team heads-up: CS, Sales, Legal (if enterprise customers affected).

Operator hourly beat (day-of, H=0 start of canary)
- H-1: Final sign-off call (15m). Confirm smoke acceptance green, obs dashboards ready, on-call roster on channel.
- H+0: Canary start (2% traffic). Post-insert check at +5m: basic health, errors, integration handshakes.
- H+15: Observe p50/p95 and error_rate_5m over 10 minutes. If anomalies, hold and escalate.
- H+30: Expand to 5% if metrics stable. Verify model-routing telemetry and kv-cache warmup curve.
- H+60: Checkpoint retro note: traffic ramp progress, any warnings, and mitigation actions.
- H+120: Expand to 25% or pre-agreed safe threshold. Run an end-to-end user scenario smoke test.
- H+240: Target full ramp if all gates green; otherwise maintain at 25% and open a deeper investigation sprint.
- H+360+: Post-ramp observation and baseline stabilization for 24 hours.

Signal catalog and gating rules (automated/observability-driven)
- Soft gate: p95 latency increase <= 12% vs baseline and error_rate_5m < 0.5%.
- Hard gate: p95 latency increase > 25% OR error_rate_5m > 2% => immediate pause and revert to previous routing.
- Backpressure: queue_depth > 80% of capacity for 5m triggers throttle policy (reduce batching, increase worker pool) and notifies infra_owner.
- Cache regression: kv-cache-hit-rate drop of >15% sustained for 10m => investigate cold-start path; consider rolling back model variant.

Compact smoke checklist (copy into runbook)
- Health endpoints: /health, /metrics ping, KV store probe.
- Model artifact checksum verification.
- A/B routing sanity: sample outputs for known prompts and compare token-level timing.
- Synthetic load: 200 concurrent short chats + 50 long-sequence in region.
- Security quick-check: recent IAM changes, key rotations audit.

Communication templates (use as Slack/Gmail snippets)
- Launch start (channel): "Canary started at H:00 — 2% global. Observability leads on deck: @obs_lead @infra_owner. Health checks in 5m."
- Escalation (DM to on-call): "Observed p95 latency +30% in US region for 10m. Pausing ramp and initiating rollback checklist. See runbook link: <link>."
- Post-launch summary (email): 1 paragraph summary, timeline of key events, user impact (if any), next steps and retro meeting link.

Rollback matrix (fast decisions)
- Tier 1 (automated): Hard gate triggers => toggled routing back to prior model variant, scale up fallback pool. Target TTR (time to revert) < 3 minutes (automation).
- Tier 2 (manual): Repeated soft-gate breaches across two regions => call with product and infra owners, consider partial rollback (regional) within 15 minutes.
- Tier 3 (escalation): New class of error (data corruption, security) => exec pager and Incident Commander.

Operational run snippets (obs queries and playbooks)
- Latency by model variant (promql): rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m]) grouped by model_variant -> alert if p95 shift >12%.
- Error stream filter: service:inference AND (status >= 500 OR timeout) grouped by route, sample stack traces.
- Cache warmup curve: kv_cache_hits / kv_cache_requests over 15m windows.

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep the hourly beat lightweight — operators will churn if too many checklist items. Focus on decisive gates.
- Have a single source-of-truth dashboard with these five widgets pinned.
- If we see region-specific anomalies, prefer regional rollback to global.

After-action and quick retro (fill within 6 hours)
- One-line outcome: shipped / paused / rolled back and why.
- Top 3 signals that mattered and what threshold adjustments we should make.
- Owners of follow-ups (bugfix, observability tweak, playbook update).
- Copy any noteworthy user-facing messages for CS to reuse.

Appendix: quick checklist copy (for pasting into a ticket)
- [ ] Owners acked in #release-2026-06-runtime
- [ ] Smoke harness green in staging
- [ ] Backup routing artifact verified
- [ ] Pager templates tested
- [ ] Slack channel created and pinned resources attached
- [ ] Observability queries loaded into shared dashboard

If anything is unclear or you want me to trim this into a single-page operator pocket sheet, ping me.

-- Priya
